Plots an log2 spaced EHA spectra

Source: R/plot_eha_log2.R
plot_eha_log2.Rd

Plot wavelet scalogram using the outcome of the eha_log2 function.

Usage

plot_eha_log2(
  eha_log2 = NULL,
  plot_opt = "Amplitude",
  lowerPeriod = NULL,
  upperPeriod = NULL,
  n.levels = 100,
  palette_name = "viridis",
  color_brewer = "viridis",
  useRaster = TRUE,
  periodlab = "Period (metres)",
  x_lab = "depth (metres)",
  keep_editable = FALSE,
  dev_new = wr_dev_new_default(),
  plot_dir = TRUE,
  add_lines = NULL,
  add_points = NULL,
  add_abline_h = NULL,
  add_abline_v = NULL,
  add_MTM_peaks = FALSE,
  add_data = TRUE,
  add_avg = FALSE,
  pval_abline = c(0.1, 0.05),
  pval_cutoff = c(0.1),
  add_MTM = FALSE,
  mtm_siglvl = 0.95,
  demean_mtm = TRUE,
  detrend_mtm = TRUE,
  padfac_mtm = 5,
  tbw_mtm = 3,
  plot_horizontal = TRUE,
  colour_brewer = NULL,
  scale = "auto"
)

Arguments

eha_log2

Evolutive harmonic analysis result to plot: the list returned by eha_log2. Required (Default=NULL gives an error).

plot_opt

Quantity shown in the spectrogram and in the average panel (character), one of "Amplitude", "Power", "Probability" (harmonic F-test probability) or "F_test" (F-test value); any other value plots the amplitude. Default="Amplitude".

lowerPeriod

Shortest period shown on the period axis, in the depth/time unit of the input record (numeric, > 0). NULL uses the shortest period of eha_log2. Default=NULL.

upperPeriod

Longest period shown on the period axis, in the depth/time unit of the input record (numeric, > lowerPeriod). NULL uses the longest period of eha_log2. Default=NULL.

n.levels

Number of colour levels of the colour scale (integer, >= 2). Default=100.

palette_name

Name of the colour palette of the power (colour) scale, a character string. Which names are valid depends on color_brewer:

  • color_brewer = "grDevices": "rainbow", "heat.colors", "terrain.colors", "topo.colors", "cm.colors", or any of the 115 hcl.colors palettes (list them with grDevices::hcl.pals()), for example "viridis", "Plasma", "Inferno", "YlOrRd", "Spectral", "Blue-Red", "Zissou 1".

  • color_brewer = "viridis": "viridis", "magma", "inferno", "plasma", "cividis", "rocket", "mako", "turbo".

  • color_brewer = "RColorBrewer": "BrBG", "PiYG", "PRGn", "PuOr", "RdBu", "RdGy", "RdYlBu", "RdYlGn", "Spectral", "Accent", "Dark2", "Paired", "Pastel1", "Pastel2", "Set1", "Set2", "Set3", "Blues", "BuGn", "BuPu", "GnBu", "Greens", "Greys", "Oranges", "OrRd", "PuBu", "PuBuGn", "PuRd", "Purples", "RdPu", "Reds", "YlGn", "YlGnBu", "YlOrBr", "YlOrRd" (also listed by wr_brewer_palettes()).

  • color_brewer = "colorRamps": "blue2green", "blue2green2red", "blue2red", "blue2yellow", "cyan2yellow", "green2red", "magenta2green", "matlab.like", "matlab.like2", "ygobb".

  • color_brewer = "scico" (all except "batlowK" need the scico package): "acton", "bam", "bamako", "bamO", "batlow", "batlowK", "batlowW", "berlin", "bilbao", "broc", "brocO", "buda", "bukavu", "cork", "corkO", "davos", "devon", "fes", "glasgow", "grayC", "hawaii", "imola", "lajolla", "lapaz", "lipari", "lisbon", "managua", "navia", "nuuk", "oleron", "oslo", "roma", "romaO", "tofino", "tokyo", "turku", "vanimo", "vik", "vikO".

Low power is drawn with the first colour of the palette and high power with the last. Default="viridis".

color_brewer

Palette family from which palette_name is taken, a character string: "grDevices", "viridis", "RColorBrewer", "colorRamps" or "scico" (the last one, except for "batlowK", needs the scico package). See palette_name for the palette names of each family. Default="viridis".

useRaster

Draw the spectrogram as a raster image (TRUE) or as vector polygons (FALSE) (logical). WARNING: plotting as a vector image is computationally intensive and gives large files. Default=TRUE.

periodlab

Label of the period axis (character). Default="Period (metres)".

x_lab

Label of the depth/time axis (character). Default="depth (metres)".

keep_editable

Keep the plot layout and graphical parameters (par) after plotting, so that extra elements can be added to the spectrogram panel with lines, points etc. (logical). With FALSE the previous par settings are restored on exit. Default=FALSE.

dev_new

Open a new plotting window for the plot (logical, TRUE or FALSE). The wavelet plots contain a raster image that needs more room than the small RStudio plot pane, which gives "figure margins too large" errors or clipped text, so a separate window is opened by default in the RStudio GUI. In every other front end (plain R, ESS, Positron, knitr, Rscript) the plot is drawn on the current device and no window is opened. Set TRUE or FALSE to force either behaviour, or set options(waverider.dev_new = TRUE/FALSE). Default=wr_dev_new_default(): TRUE in the RStudio GUI, FALSE elsewhere.

plot_dir

Direction of the depth/time axis (logical). TRUE plots increasing depth/time values from left to right (or bottom to top when plot_horizontal=FALSE); FALSE reverses the axis. Default=TRUE.

add_lines

Lines to draw on the spectrogram: a matrix or data frame with depth/time in column 1 and, in each further column, period values (same unit as the period axis) of one line; NULL draws none. Default=NULL.

add_points

Points to draw on the spectrogram: a matrix or data frame with depth/time in column 1 and, in each further column, period values of one series of points; NULL draws none. Default=NULL.

add_abline_h

Numeric vector of positions of horizontal lines, e.g. c(2, 3, 5, 6): periods when plot_horizontal=TRUE, depth/time values when plot_horizontal=FALSE; NULL draws none. Default=NULL.

add_abline_v

Numeric vector of positions of vertical lines, e.g. c(2, 3, 5, 6): depth/time values when plot_horizontal=TRUE (also drawn on the data panel), periods when plot_horizontal=FALSE; NULL draws none. Default=NULL.

add_MTM_peaks

Run a multitaper (MTM) analysis of the whole record (mtm) and draw the periods of its significant peaks (at mtm_siglvl) as dotted lines on the spectrogram (and in red on the MTM panels); the MTM result with a Peak column (1 = significant peak) is then returned invisibly (logical). Default=FALSE.

add_data

Plot the input record in a panel beside the spectrogram (logical). Default=TRUE.

add_avg

Plot the average of the plotted quantity (plot_opt) over the record in a panel beside the spectrogram (logical). Default=FALSE.

pval_abline

Not used; kept for compatibility with older versions (numeric vector of p-values). Default=c(0.1, 0.05).

pval_cutoff

Not used; kept for compatibility with older versions (numeric p-value). Default=c(0.1).

add_MTM

Add three panels beside the spectrogram with the MTM power spectrum of the whole record (with its AR(1) confidence levels), the AR(1) confidence level and the harmonic F-test confidence level (in %), computed with mtm (logical). Default=FALSE.

mtm_siglvl

Significance level used to select the MTM peaks (numeric, between 0 and 1; siglevel of mtm). Default=0.95.

demean_mtm

Remove the mean from the record before the MTM analysis (logical; demean of mtm). Default=TRUE.

detrend_mtm

Remove a linear trend from the record before the MTM analysis (logical; detrend of mtm). Default=TRUE.

padfac_mtm

Zero-padding factor of the MTM analysis (numeric, >= 1; padfac of mtm). Default=5.

tbw_mtm

Time-bandwidth product of the MTM analysis (numeric, e.g. 2, 3 or 4; tbw of mtm); higher values give smoother spectra with lower frequency resolution. Default=3.

plot_horizontal

Orientation of the plot (logical): TRUE puts depth/time on the x axis and period on the y axis; FALSE puts depth/time on the y axis and period on the x axis. Default=TRUE.

colour_brewer

British spelling of color_brewer, with the same options; if given (not NULL) it overrides color_brewer. Default=NULL.

scale

Spacing of the colour breaks of the colour scale, as in all image plots of the package (character): "quantile" (histogram-equalised), "log", "sqrt", "linear" or "auto" (logarithmic for mostly empty maps or values spanning more than three orders of magnitude, quantiles otherwise); see plot_wavelet. Default="auto".

Value

The output is a plot of a EHA spectra. if add_MTM_peaks = TRUE then the output of the MTM analysis will given as matrix

References

Angi Roesch and Harald Schmidbauer (2018). WaveletComp: Computational Wavelet Analysis. R package version 1.1. https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=WaveletComp

S.R. Meyers, 2012, Seeing Red in Cyclic Stratigraphy: Spectral Noise Estimation for Astrochronology: Paleoceanography, 27, PA3228, <doi:10.1029/2012PA002307>

S.R. Meyers, 2019 Cyclostratigraphy and the problem of astrochronologic testing, Earth-Science Reviews, Volume 190, <doi.org/10.1016/j.earscirev.2018.11.015.>

Author

Code based on the wt.image" functions of the 'WaveletComp' R package The EHA and MTM analysis parts are from the astrochron R package of Meyers et al., (2012)

Examples

# \donttest{
#Example 1. A plot of a wavelet spectra using the Total Solar Irradiance
# data set of Steinhilber et al., (2012)

TSI_eha_log2 <- eha_log2(data = TSI,
win =  8192,
tbw = 4,
demean = TRUE,
detrend = TRUE,
upperPeriod = 8192,
lowerPeriod = 50,
pad = NULL,
padding = "noise")

plot_eha_log2(
eha_log2 = TSI_eha_log2,
plot_opt = "Amplitude",
lowerPeriod = 50,
upperPeriod = 8192,
n.levels = 100,
palette_name = "rainbow",
color_brewer = "grDevices",
useRaster = TRUE,
periodlab = "Period (metres)",
x_lab = "depth (metres)",
keep_editable = FALSE,
dev_new = TRUE,
plot_dir = TRUE,
add_lines = NULL,
add_points = NULL,
add_abline_h = NULL,
add_abline_v = NULL,
add_MTM_peaks = FALSE,
add_data = TRUE,
add_avg = FALSE,
add_MTM = FALSE,
mtm_siglvl = 0.95,
demean_mtm = TRUE,
detrend_mtm = TRUE,
padfac_mtm = 5,
tbw_mtm = 3,
plot_horizontal = TRUE)


#Example 2. A plot of a wavelet spectra using the magnetic susceptibility
#data set of Pas et al., (2018)
mag_eha_log2 <- eha_log2(data = mag,
win =  50,
tbw = 4,
demean = TRUE,
detrend = TRUE,
upperPeriod = 50,
lowerPeriod = 1,
pad = NULL,
padding = "noise")

plot_eha_log2(
eha_log2 = mag_eha_log2,
plot_opt = "Amplitude",
lowerPeriod = 1,
upperPeriod = 50,
n.levels = 100,
palette_name = "rainbow",
color_brewer = "grDevices",
useRaster = TRUE,
periodlab = "Period (metres)",
x_lab = "depth (metres)",
keep_editable = FALSE,
dev_new = TRUE,
plot_dir = TRUE,
add_lines = NULL,
add_points = NULL,
add_abline_h = NULL,
add_abline_v = NULL,
add_MTM_peaks = FALSE,
add_data = TRUE,
add_avg = FALSE,
add_MTM = FALSE,
mtm_siglvl = 0.95,
demean_mtm = TRUE,
detrend_mtm = TRUE,
padfac_mtm = 5,
tbw_mtm = 3,
plot_horizontal = TRUE)



#Example 3. A plot of a wavelet spectra using the greyscale
# data set of Zeeden et al., (2013)
grey_eha_log2 <- eha_log2(data = grey,
win =  20,
tbw = 4,
demean = TRUE,
detrend = TRUE,
upperPeriod = 20,
lowerPeriod = 1,
pad = NULL,
padding = "noise")


plot_eha_log2(
eha_log2 = grey_eha_log2,
plot_opt = "Amplitude",
lowerPeriod = 1,
upperPeriod = 20,
n.levels = 100,
palette_name = "rainbow",
color_brewer = "grDevices",
useRaster = TRUE,
periodlab = "Period (metres)",
x_lab = "depth (metres)",
keep_editable = FALSE,
dev_new = TRUE,
plot_dir = TRUE,
add_lines = NULL,
add_points = NULL,
add_abline_h = NULL,
add_abline_v = NULL,
add_MTM_peaks = FALSE,
add_data = TRUE,
add_avg = FALSE,
add_MTM = FALSE,
mtm_siglvl = 0.95,
demean_mtm = TRUE,
detrend_mtm = TRUE,
padfac_mtm = 5,
tbw_mtm = 3,
plot_horizontal = TRUE)
